shots.description: Hook: the whole globe in dark space, an inland region outlined by a bright glowing ice-blue line with 3 to 4 fainter offset contour lines around it (distance bands), the ocean navy, the land warm dark grey with relief. The region shrinks toward one point while the camera zooms down onto it; a candy-striped red/cream pole marker with a small orange flag and a thin ellipse ring at its foot drops onto the point. The map recolours: the country containing the point fills ochre-orange with a thin light border, a neighbouring country fills pale grey, the shared border glows hot magenta; white uppercase country labels with dark shadows pop in; a two-line white title (place name, smaller second line) types in at the top (y about 15%). Word-by-word white captions at about 71% of the height.

shots.description: One continuous map camera over the same globe. Overlays fade; a big rolling counter (heavy rounded sans, gold with dark outline, small 'KM' after it) appears top-left at y about 21% while a gold line grows from the marker to the nearest coast, then a gold distance circle sweeps round the marker touching the coast; the camera pulls back so the circle reads on the globe; a comparison line between two named cities (small gold node dots, white uppercase labels) gets its own counter; a short white tag ('N KM SHORT') where the line stops short of the coast. Twist: the camera pans north along the circle to a coastal water feature, its outline traced in bright cyan, an italic serif ice-blue label names it; a year ruler (ticks, decade numbers, gold pointer, the year in large orange serif) slides in at the top; the land around turns pale ice blue (the feature recounted as ocean), new contour bands appear and the marker splits into two new markers. Then an orange glowing outline of the country, orange circles with ripple nodes where they touch coasts, the counter rolls to the new value in orange.

story.summary: A map explainer that makes one geographic superlative concrete: it zooms from the globe to the spot, measures it with a rolling number and a distance ring, compares it with a familiar trip, corrects it, then flips to the opposite spot and shows the two numbers are almost equal.
story.hook: 0 to 4 s: the whole globe with one region glowing in contour bands and the claim "this is the furthest you can get from X"; by 4 s the camera has zoomed onto a marker and the place is named on a coloured map.
highlights: 9 to 12 s: a big gold counter rolls up while a line grows to the coast: the number lands with motion, not as text
12 to 15 s: a familiar city-to-city distance drawn on the same map with its own counter makes the number feel huge
16 to 34 s: a "but" twist with a year ruler: the spot moves and the counter changes colour and value, so the viewer learns the number is a measurement, not a given
42 to 52 s: two numbers side by side in gold and ice blue with two nearly equal rings: the surprise is visual before it is spoken
